cur:catacombs-ravenna-traditio-legis-mus.summary: In a calm, spacious composition Christ, nimbed and standing on a mound, hands the Law to an apostle, between palms and further figures; the ends of the chest show Daniel among the lions and the raising of Lazarus. The broad, airy design is typical of the sculpture of Ravenna in its imperial age.
facts: The museum label recorded on Commons gives its provenance as the church of San Giovanni Battista, Ravenna, and dates it to the early 5th century.
Commons has separate photographs of its Daniel and Lazarus scenes.

cur:monumental-san-doubting-thomas.summary: Before a closed doorway, the risen Christ stands among the apostles in white, raising his right arm to reveal the wound in his side as Thomas bends forward to touch it. The scene closes the Passion and Resurrection sequence of the south wall with Christ's bodily presence among his disciples.
facts: On the south wall the thirteen Passion and Resurrection scenes show Christ bearded; the cycle omits both the Flagellation and the Crucifixion.
The scenes were not arranged in biblical order but are thought to follow the Gospel readings of the Lenten liturgy in Theodoric's palace church.

walters:W.185.15R.summary: Inside a gilded initial D, the Virgin in a deep blue mantle holds the Christ Child close against her cheek. The initial opens the Hours of the Virgin, under the red heading 'Hore de domina nostra', and the page is framed by a rich border of gold and coloured foliage inhabited by small creatures. It is an intimate image placed at the start of the most-used prayers of the book.
walters:W.185.15R.scripture: Psalm 51:15 (text on the page: 'Domine labia mea aperies')
facts: The book is named after Franchoise de Doffinnes, who owned it in the late 16th century; her family's later history is recorded on its final folios.

Its calendar follows the Use of Utrecht and its Hours of the Virgin largely the Use of the Windesheim Congregation, pointing to a Dutch origin; it contains both Latin and Dutch texts and twelve full-page miniatures by the Master of Walters 185.
walters:W.185.15R.notes: Museum date (1400–1425) applies to the whole Book of Hours; the date in our data (8th century) was an import error.
